receiver.message_back: Counsel, Defendant’s response is facially deficient: it asserts only boilerplate objections, promises production without specifying timing or categories, and states that an “attached” privilege log identifies withheld documents, but no such log was provided. Please confirm by return that Defendant will produce all responsive documents and a compliant privilege log by a date certain, or we will seek appropriate relief and fees.

drafter.private_reasoning: Opposing counsel has a strong procedural point: the draft says a privilege log is attached when it was not, and production timing/categories are vague. To reduce motion risk and fees exposure while preserving objections, I revised the response to provide a date certain, clarify that production will be made subject to objections, identify the categories to be produced in general terms, and commit to serving a compliant privilege log for documents withheld on privilege/work-product grounds. I did not include any confidential settlement/pricing information.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Thank you for your note. Defendant will serve amended responses and begin a rolling production of responsive, non-privileged documents. Defendant expects to complete its production by November 17, 2026, subject to any later-discovered documents and the parties’ continuing obligations. Defendant will also serve a privilege log by that date for documents withheld on privilege or work-product grounds.

We do not agree that fees or motion practice are warranted, but we have revised the responses to address your stated concerns and to move discovery forward.

Best,
Counsel for Defendant

edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff's First Requests for Production as set forth below. These responses are made after a reasonable inquiry based on information presently available to Defendant and are subject to supplementation under the applicable rules.
edits.name: Preliminary Statement

edits.text: 1. GENERAL OBJECTIONS. Defendant objects to each request to the extent it seeks documents or information protected by the attorney-client privilege, the work-product doctrine, or any other applicable privilege or protection. Defendant further objects to each request to the extent it is overbroad, unduly burdensome, disproportionate to the needs of the case, seeks documents not within Defendant's possession, custody, or control, or seeks information that is not relevant to any party's claim or defense. These objections are preserved and are not waived by Defendant's agreement to produce responsive, non-privileged documents.
edits.name: General Objections

edits.text: 2. PRODUCTION. Subject to and without waiving the foregoing objections, Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control, including documents sufficient to show the communications, agreements, and records responsive to Plaintiff's First Requests for Production. Defendant will make its production on a rolling basis and will complete production by November 17, 2026, subject to supplementation if additional responsive, non-privileged documents are later identified.
edits.name: Production

edits.text: 3. PRIVILEGE LOG. Defendant is withholding documents, if any, on the basis of attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, or other applicable protection. Defendant will serve a privilege log compliant with the applicable rules by November 17, 2026, identifying documents withheld on such grounds, except for categories of documents not required to be logged under the applicable rules or any agreement of the parties.
edits.name: Privilege Log

edits.text: 4. RESERVATION. Defendant reserves the right to supplement or amend these responses and its production consistent with the applicable rules and any orders of the Court.
edits.name: Reservation
